body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)
body.estimand_functional: The established data-only estimating functional is \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\).  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), it satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\le Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},\] while the corresponding minimax risk satisfies \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\] The two powers coincide when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\); the sharper rough-nuisance functional remains the subject of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give a pointwise H\"older-CATE nuisance-smoothness frontier under bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class; the displayed lower construction in Definition 1 uses a covariate density supported on a perforated set.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the proved oracle converse and total first-order estimator give \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At bounded overlap \((\kappa=0)\), this becomes a rigorous exact-uniform bracket and closes to \(R_n\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), without a logarithm, when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  The sharper rough-nuisance rate, its critical logarithms, and its same-class full-support product-mixture converse remain open.

project_justification.gap: The closest published pointwise CATE frontier assumes bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class, and its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  That witness does not prove a nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform design, while the overlapping-frame replacement presently lacks a valid fixed-\(n\) product-mixture comparison.
project_justification.niche: Exactly uniform covariates and a known polynomial overlap geometry isolate a local treatment-scarcity experiment.  The current contribution separates what is already certified---the oracle benchmark, an explicit first-order data-only rate, and the full smooth-nuisance slice---from the unresolved higher-order rough-nuisance frontier.
project_justification.fill: The paper provides a total finite-operation estimator and the honest all-regime bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\).  It proves oracle attainment whenever \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), including the exact-uniform bounded-overlap rate with no logarithm, and records the specific mixture and smoothness obstructions that prevent a sharper claim when \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\).

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 1, is the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier.  Its density-qualified class and displayed perforated-support lower witness motivate the conjectured nuisance elbow but do not establish that lower bound for the singleton uniform design used here.  The present Theorem 3 therefore proves only the bracket supplied by the exact-uniform oracle converse and first-order upper bound, becoming sharp when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies bounded-overlap local-polynomial R-learner motivation, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate higher-order projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The rough-nuisance lower-bound routes fail for structural reasons not repaired by the current core.  Write \(S=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\).  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^S\) have H\"older scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\), which diverges as \(\ell\downarrow0\).  Overlapping smooth squared frames repair the transition regularity but violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and their shared signs generate nonzero multi-observation cross terms.  Filling the perforated transition holes instead leaves a product-experiment contribution of order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which diverges at the proposed nuisance rate below the elbow.  Noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces create additional compensation regularity issues for \(\kappa>0\).
body.honest_scope: The established result is the parameterized bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), attained on the upper side by a total clipped three-block estimator.  It is sharp and equals the oracle rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  In particular, for \(\kappa=0\) this smooth-nuisance slice has rate \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) without a logarithm.  For \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), the higher-order upper rate, matching exact-uniform lower bound, oracle-penalty classification, and critical logarithms remain open; no Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman rate is claimed for that slice.
